spatial_claims.claim: Assume AB >= DE; if AB = DE then triangles are congruent by I.26; otherwise AB > DE
P is placed on segment AB with AP = DE, so P lies strictly between A and B (since AB > DE > 0)
PQ is drawn through P parallel to BC, meeting AC at Q, with Q between A and C
Angle PAQ = angle BAC because P lies on ray AB and Q lies on ray AC (same vertex angle at A)
Angle APQ = angle ABC by I.29 (corresponding angles with PQ parallel to BC)
PQ parallel to BC cuts sides AB and AC proportionally: AP:PB = AQ:QC (VI.2)
AP + PB = AB since P is between A and B
AQ + QC = AC since Q is between A and C
(AP+PB):(AQ+QC) = AP:AQ by V.12, hence AB:AC = DE:DF

configuration_map: Triangle ABC with vertices A, B, C. Triangle DEF with vertices D, E, F. Equiangular correspondence: angle BAC = angle EDF, angle ABC = angle DEF, angle ACB = angle DFE. Point P on segment AB with AP = DE, strictly between A and B (since AB > DE). Point Q on segment AC, the intersection of the line through P parallel to BC with side AC; Q lies strictly between A and C. Triangle APQ is congruent to triangle DEF (by ASA via I.26). Line PQ is parallel to side BC and lies entirely within triangle ABC. The configuration is a standard parallel intercept within a triangle with no auxiliary points outside the triangle or ambiguous positioning.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The construction places P strictly between A and B and Q strictly between A and C via a parallel line, with no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior ambiguity, and no ray-ordering issues. Every proportion and angle identity follows directly from the established positions. The proof is a clean parallel-line proportionality argument with no configuration tension.
